summary: Kang-nam Oh works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and under doctoral supervisor Yün-hua Jan (attested 1976), and held a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).

Kang-yuan Sung specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. Sung earned an MA at the University of Calgary, studying under MA supervisor Anthony W. Barber (attested 1999) as well as teachers Anne Moore and Leslie S. Kawamura.

Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied under Takamatsu Yoshie and at the University of Paris (~1928–1931), later serving as an appointee (嘱託) at Tokyo National Museum.

Kanji Tamura (born 1944) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at Rissho University, including part-time lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and associate professor (attested 2026).

Kanoko Tanaka is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She studied under traditional teacher Acharya Tulsi and served as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).
Kansei Tamura (1928–2018) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1962) and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1962).
Kanti Chandra Pandey (1903–1971) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He founded the University of Lucknow and held a post there (attested 1950).

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) worked in Indology and history/archaeology, studying at Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University (PhD). She taught at Delhi and BHU, founded IGNCA (serving as member secretary, Academic Director, and chairperson), and chaired the India International Centre.

Karam Tej Singh Sarao (born 1955) works in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Delhi and Cambridge (PhD under F. R. Allchin and K. R. Norman), he taught at Kirori Mal College and became professor at Delhi in 1995.

Karandagolle Sobhitha specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. After earning an MPhil at the University of Peradeniya (-2018), Sobhitha served there as temporary lecturer (2011–2015) and as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at Bhiksu University of Sri Lanka (2015–2021).
Karel Glaser (1845–1913) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin and Vienna (PhD ~1883 under Georg Bühler). He worked as a teacher at Stadtgymnasium Trieste from 1880 to 1900.

Karel Oštir (1888–1973) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Vienna under Paul Kretschmer and earned a PhD at Graz (1919) under Rudolf Meringer. He spent his career at the University of Ljubljana, serving as ordinary professor (1932–1958).
Karel Přikryl (1718–1785) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as a teacher at Rachol Seminary (~1756–1760) and became Rector of the Jesuit College in Hradec Králové in 1768.

Karel Werner (1925–2019) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, earning a PhD at Palacký University. He taught at Palacký, Cambridge, and Masaryk University, and served as lecturer in Indian philosophy at Durham University (1969–1990).

Karen Christina Lang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, LTWA, and the University of Washington (PhD 1983 under David Seyfort Ruegg), and served as professor at the University of Virginia.
Karen Katsumoto specializes in Buddhist studies. She held posts as a part-time lecturer at Hanazono University (attested 2006) and as a lecturer at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) worked in religious studies. She studied at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University, and served as professor of anthropology at Drew University (~1976–2009).
Karen Nelson Villanueva works in religious studies. She earned a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies and studied under traditional teachers Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.
Karen Nero held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (~1998–2007) and the University of Otago.

Karen O'Brien-Kop works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD and served as senior teaching fellow at SOAS, later lecturing at the University of Roehampton (attested 2020) and King's College London (2022).
